# The same request on port 80, in the clear:

$ curl -i http://ca-hello-dev-scus-001.<env>.southcentralus.azurecontainerapps.io/

HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
location: https://ca-hello-dev-scus-001.<env>.southcentralus.azurecontainerapps.io/
content-length: 0

# allow_insecure_connections = false is doing the work in that second
# response. Left at its default, the ingress still serves HTTPS -- but it
# ALSO answers port 80 with a 200, and a client that gets a 200 in the clear
# has no reason to ever upgrade. The 301 is the difference between "HTTPS is
# available" and "HTTPS is the only way in".
#
# The environment subdomain is elided here; it is generated per environment
# and appears in full in the portal figures.
